offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The evidence ties the 100x overcharges to the payments-api deploy at 19:03:19 that set CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, and rolling that deploy back fits the cause.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payments-api deploy at 19:03:19Z set CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. payments-api still stores amounts in cents, for example amount_cents=1396 for $13.96. With this setting it sends that cent value to fake-provider as dollars, so every charge since the deploy is made at 100x our amount ($1,396.00 instead of $13.96). Our payments table keeps the right cents value while the provider records the inflated charge, and that is what fails payments_match_provider. The ledger books from the provider's webhooks, so it agrees with the provider: matches_provider and ledger_balanced pass. Only our payments disagree.

evidence.shows: The symptom is confirmed. Only payments_match_provider fails, with 63 findings. Each finding is a provider charge exactly 100x our amount: pmt_000245 is 1396 cents with us and 139600 at the provider, and pmt_000246 is 12165 with us and 1216500 at the provider. The other invariants pass, and the mismatched ids run in sequence from pmt_000245.
payments-api was redeployed at 19:03:19Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, about 1.5 minutes after every other service was created at 19:01:52Z. It is the only recent change in settings.

pmt_000245, the first mismatched payment, succeeded at 19:03:20.642Z, one second after the deploy, with amount_cents=1396. This places the bad charges after the deploy. A refund of 1396 cents was then made on it, which is only 1% of the provider charge.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings before the latest deploy, which should be CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT in cents, so that new charges go to the provider at the right amount. Afterwards, repair the about 63 charges already overcharged: refund the excess at the provider, 99x our amount less any refunds already made, then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api is recreated, so payment and refund requests pause briefly while it restarts. Charges made before the rollback stay overcharged at the provider until they are refunded. The rollback stops new damage and repairs nothing. The evidence leaves some points open. I did not confirm the setting's value before the deploy; it is presumably cents. I did not confirm that no payments before 19:03:19 are affected, although the findings start at pmt_000245, right after the deploy. I did not inspect the amount on the provider request in a trace.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the settings it has now (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). Then rerun money_check to compare.
